title: Affine direct image of quasi-coherent modules on algebraic spaces commutes with arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume $f$ is affine: it is representable and, for every affine scheme $V\to Y$, the scheme $X\times_Y V$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, with projections $h:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use tensor pullback and module direct image for the canonical ringed etale topoi [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Then $f_*F$ is quasi-coherent, and the canonical natural map
$$\beta_F:g^*f_*F\longrightarrow f'_*h^*F$$
is an isomorphism. Here $\beta_F$ is adjoint under $f'^*\dashv f'_*$ to
$$f'^*g^*f_*F\simeq h^*f^*f_*F\xrightarrow{h^*\epsilon_F}h^*F,$$
where $\epsilon_F$ is the counit and the first arrow is the canonical composition comparison for tensor pullbacks [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]. There is no flatness, finite-type, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis on $g$, and no finite-type or finite-presentation hypothesis on $F$.

source.place: Tag 07U8, lemma-affine-base-change, the quasi-coherent direct image and ordinary degree-zero base-change assertion; canonical map given in the discussion and base-change morphism preceding equation-base-change-diagram.

proof.text: For an affine etale chart $u:V\to Y$, set $U=X\times_YV$, $p:U\to V$ and $E=F|_U$. The hypothesis on $f$ makes $U$ affine and $p$ affine: an affine scheme test over $V$ is also an affine scheme test over $Y$. Restricting a local presentation shows $E$ is quasi-coherent. Etale direct-image restriction identifies $(f_*F)|_V$ with $p_*E$. By affine-morphism permanence $p$ is quasi-compact and separated. Apply the scheme Zariski/etale equivalence to $E$, and clause (1) of scheme affine pushforward/base change to its Zariski counterpart. The direct-image comparison in that equivalence makes $p_*E$ quasi-coherent on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$. Thus $f_*F$ has local presentations on the affine etale charts, which cover $Y$, and is quasi-coherent by the definition.

source.place: Tag 07U8, lemma-affine-base-change, proof and equation-representable-higher-direct-image; coherent.tex Tag 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change.

proof.text: Choose a covering of $Y$ by affine etale schemes $V_i$. Base change gives an etale covering $W_i=Y'\times_YV_i\to Y'$. Cover each algebraic space $W_i$ by affine etale schemes $V'_{ij}$. Composition of etale coverings shows that $u'_{ij}:V'_{ij}\to Y'$ form a covering. There is a scheme morphism $a:V'_{ij}\to V_i$, with no flatness requirement. Write $U_i=X\times_YV_i$, $U'_{ij}=U_i\times_{V_i}V'_{ij}$, $p_i:U_i\to V_i$, $p'_{ij}:U'_{ij}\to V'_{ij}$ and $b:U'_{ij}\to U_i$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $U'_{ij}$ with $X'\times_{Y'}V'_{ij}$. Both $U_i$ and $U'_{ij}$ are affine schemes, the latter by affine scheme base-change permanence. In particular every square now used for the scheme theorem is a square of schemes; we have not assumed that $Y'$ itself is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 07U8, lemma-affine-base-change, proof and equation-representable-higher-direct-image; coherent.tex Tag 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change.

proof.text: Fix one of these squares and put $E=F|_U$. The restriction comparisons for etale direct image, together with the tensor-pullback composition comparison for the equal composites $g u'=u a$, identify the restriction of the source of $\beta_F$ with $a^*p_*E$. Applying the same direct-image restriction to $f'$ and tensor composition to $h$ identifies its target with $p'_*b^*E$. These comparisons use etale pullback as restriction; their direct-image section maps are identities. Now pass to Zariski quasi-coherent modules on the four schemes. Tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence, and $p,p'$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and separated. Therefore all four pullback/direct-image comparisons of the scheme Zariski/etale equivalence apply. Denote the Zariski counterpart of $E$ by $H$. The two objects become $a^*p_*H$ and $p'_*b^*H$.

source.place: Tag 07U8, lemma-affine-base-change, proof and equation-representable-higher-direct-image; coherent.tex Tag 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change.

proof.text:
Check the map under these identifications, not just the objects. The chart-unit formula for tensor pullback says its unit sends a section $m$ to $1\otimes m$; the triangle identity and linearity then force the counit to send a local tensor $c\otimes m$ to $c$ times the restricted section $m$. Direct-image restriction leaves that section unchanged. The composition comparison sends $c\otimes(d\otimes m)$ to $c\,d\otimes m$ with $d$ pulled back along the relevant ring map. For $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ and $M=H(U)$, the adjoint defining the restricted $\beta_F$ consequently gives
$$R'\otimes_R M\longrightarrow(R'\otimes_R B)\otimes_B M,\qquad r'\otimes m\longmapsto(r'\otimes1)\otimes m.$$
Indeed its adjoint sends $c\otimes(r'\otimes m)$ to $c(r'\otimes1)\otimes m$; precomposing with the adjunction unit sets $c=1$. The Zariski/etale pullback comparison is itself specified by the module adjunctions and units and counits, so this computation applies through that comparison as well. These are local tensor representatives, and linearity and sheafification determine the maps from them. This is exactly the canonical map, including its direction, specified in clause (1) of scheme affine pushforward/base change.

source.place: Tag 07U8, lemma-affine-base-change, proof and equation-representable-higher-direct-image; coherent.tex Tag 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change.

proof.text: Clause (1) of scheme affine pushforward/base change makes the map computed in step 4 an isomorphism for every $R\to R'$ and every $B$-module $M$. Its inverse has the balanced formula $(r'\otimes b)\otimes m\mapsto r'\otimes bm$; the composites on pure tensors are identities. Hence $\beta_F$ restricts to an isomorphism on every $V'_{ij}$. For any object of $Y'_{\mathrm{et}}$, pull back this covering. Given a section of the target, apply the local inverse on the covering pieces; these sections agree on overlaps because they are inverses of the restrictions of the same map, and uniqueness follows from local injectivity. The sheaf axiom glues them to its unique inverse image. This constructs an inverse to $\beta_F$. All comparisons and the tensor formula commute with module maps, so the result is the stated natural comparison. Neither the tensor inverse nor the chart construction used flatness, finite type, finite presentation, or Noetherian assumptions.
